UNION MINISTER SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA HOLDS MEETING IN MAMIT

882/2022-2023 Mamit 13th June, 2022: Shri Parshottam Rupala, Hon'ble Union Cabinet Minister, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Govt of India, today held an interaction with Government Officials and beneficiaries of various Central Schemes within Mamit town at the DC Conference Hall, Mamit.

In today's meeting, chaired by Pu Lalnunhlua, District Deputy Commissioner, Pu Lalsanglura, Nodal Officer for the Aspirational District Programme, presented a detailed report on various initiatives under the Aspirational District Programme using a PowerPoint presentation. This was followed by a discussion on the progress made and various future plans/areas requiring focus.

Shri Parshottam Rupala, Union Minister, explained the purpose of his visit to Mamit District and the interaction, stating that he came to monitor whether the various Central Schemes are being implemented successfully and effectively for the benefit of the district's residents, and to understand and help resolve any difficulties faced. He urged the District Concern Officers to study the various Government initiative programmes and to make efforts to ensure that the beneficiaries truly benefit from them.

As Mamit District is an Aspirational District, the Central Government has made arrangements for medical treatment of critical illnesses with bills claimable up to Rs 5 Lakhs. He mentioned that out of 50,000 selected people in Mamit District, 30,000 have already been selected to receive this benefit, and efforts are underway to ensure the remaining 20,000 also receive it. He stated that PM-Kisan can be applied for by those who possess an Aadhaar Card, land, and a Bank Account, and urged the concerned departments to make efforts so that as many farmers as possible in Mamit District can benefit from this scheme.

The Union Minister stated that he would follow up as much as possible on the difficulties and needs presented by the Government Officials and Beneficiaries during today's interaction.

During this session, an interaction followed by a question-and-answer session was held with the concerned Officials and Beneficiaries under various Central Schemes, including AYUSHMAN BHARAT - Health & Wellness, Ayushman Bharat - Jan Arogya Yojana, e-Transaction, Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), PM Street Vendor'

raw_text:
DRAFT ELECTORAL ROLL 2020 RELEASED IN LAWNGTLAI

The draft electoral roll for 2020 for the three Assembly constituencies in Lawngtlai District was released yesterday (16.12.2019) by the Lawngtlai District Election Officer and Deputy Commissioner of Lawngtlai, Pi Shashanka Ala, IAS, in her office chamber. The draft roll was immediately handed over to representatives of political parties.

According to the released draft electoral roll, in 36-Tuichawng (ST) A/C, there are 15,852 male voters and 15,520 female voters, making a total of 31,372 voters; in 37-Lawngtlai West (ST) A/C, there are 13,524 male voters and 13,402 female voters, making a total of 26,926 voters; in 38-Lawngtlai East (ST) A/C, there are 11,626 male voters and 12,374 female voters, making a total of 24,000 voters. Across the three assembly constituencies, there are 41,002 male voters and 41,296 female voters, making a total of 82,298 voters.

For the upcoming summary revision, the period for filing claims and objections is open until January 15 of the new year. The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on February 7, 2020.

Along with this, 8 new polling stations have been added to the existing 62 polling stations in the Tuichawng constituency, bringing the total to 70 polling stations; 1 new polling station has been added to the existing 68 polling stations in Lawngtlai West, bringing the total to 69 polling stations; and with 7 new polling stations added to the existing 35 in Lawngtlai East, there are now 42 polling stations. Consequently, there will be a total of 181 polling stations across the three constituencies within Lawngtlai District.

CHILDREN’S WEEK CELEBRATED IN MAMIT
Today, a 'Fun Day' programme was held at the GSA Playground in Mamit to launch Children’s Week under the theme ‘Happy Childhood’, organized by the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit District.

Pu Shashank Jaiswal IPS, Superintendent of Police, Mamit, inaugurated the event and expressed his gratitude to the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit. He commended their initiative, stating that organizing such an event for the children of Mamit to have a joyful time is highly commendable and wise. He remarked that the safety and happiness of the children in our land lie in everyone's hands, emphasizing the importance of cooperation and unity among adults and the community. He added that if children in Mamit District face any difficulties, the Mamit Police are always ready to assist them at any time. Encouraging the children to have a memorable and joyful time, he urged all attendees to use this occasion to further strengthen child protection efforts.

The programme was chaired by Pi Vanlalruati, PO(IC), DCPU. Dr. R. Lalrinhlua, DCPO, also spoke on the purpose of organizing the Fun Day for the children of Mamit town, highlighting the importance of giving children more free time and space. He stated that since children are the future leaders of our land, nurturing them with care is our responsibility.

During this Fun Day, the DCPU engaged the children with various recreational activities such as a Bouncy Castle, Trampoline, See-Saw, Mega Blocks, and a Ball Pool, along with various games including Spin the Wheel, Ball Kick, Dart Game, Cup Game, Ball Score, a Photo Booth, a Talent Hunt, and Bow and Arrow. Child Care Institutions also set up various stalls, offering these recreational activities for the children to enjoy free of charge. After I leave the house, out of sheer curiosity, they play with the eraser; then, when I return, I find out that they have done something wrong. Their wrongdoing is merely a violation of a family rule, and nothing has entered into them. However, next time, suppose I leave a bottle containing a very dangerous medicine at home and tell the children, "Do not drink this under any circumstances." After I leave the house, they find that the bottle is very fun to play with — and in the very end, they drink the dangerous medicine containing poison. Right here, they have not only violated the family rule and disobeyed my command, but worse than that, some dangerous poison has also entered into them. This is exactly what happened when Adam ate the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil on that day. He not only disobeyed what God had forbidden, but he also let Satan's life enter into him. Right there, the inside of man became extremely complicated; in addition to the good, righteous, and upright human life he had in the beginning, he also came to possess the ruined and sinful life of Satan.

source: COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER-IN LUNGLEIAH AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING HAWNG No.4122/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 26 th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana chuan vawiin khan Electric Veng, Lungleiah NABARD sum cheng nuai 1082.93 senga ruahman Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building a hawng. Hawnna inkhawm Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi kaihhruaiah Dr R Lalthangliana chuan Lunglei khawpui chhunga hmasawnna ruhrel liantham, khawtlang tana chhenfakawm tak leh eizawnna kawnga tangkai taka hman theih tur Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building zawhfel a ni chu lawmawm tiin a buaipuitu Commerce & Industries thawktute, building sa tu te leh Electric Veng Lunglei khawtlang te chungah lawmthu a sawi a. C&I Department hnuaiah hmalakna hrang hrang kalpui mek zel anih thu sawiin Lunglei Supermarket sakna tur cheng nuai 1400 NEC atanga sanction hmuh anih thu sawiin Bangladesh ram nena kan insumdawn tawnna atana ruahman Integrated Check Post (ICP), Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung ti hlawhtling turin Department chuan theihtawp a chhuah mek zel thu a sawi a ni. A Department chan dangte hnuaia hmalaknte pawh sawilangin Minister chuan MZU Southern Campus atan DPR cheng vaibelchhe 400 sawrkar laipuiah thehluh tawh niin chak taka bawhzui mek a ni a, MZU Southern Campus tana hman lailawk tur Engineering College building chei that hna pawh thawh mek a ni, a ti a. Civil Hospital Lungleia Trauma Centre sak pawh zawh fel thuai beisei anih thu sawiin Multipurpose Laboratory Building, NEC sum cheng nuai 300 a ruahman mek pawh nakum kum tir lama zawhfel beisei anih thu a sawi. Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC) chungchang pawh sawiin Minister chuan Municipal body chak tak enkawlna hnuaiah Lunglei khawpui chuan kawng hrang hrangin hmasawnna a nei dawn a ni, a ti. He huna khualzahawm Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng chuan Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building hawn theiha peih fel a ni ta chu Pathian malsawmna ropui tak a ni tiin he hmasawnna ruhrel neih theihna tura sulsutute thawhrimna leh thahnemngaihna rah a ni, a ti a. He building ti hlawhtling tura bultan tu Pu Joseph Lalhimpuia chungah leh a hmun phal taka petu Electric Veng YMA te chungah lawmthu a sawi a ni. He building sak enkawltu AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl atangin Technical Report ngaihtlak a ni a. Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure hi NABARD, RIDF XXIII hnuaia project niin total project cost hi Rs. 1082.93 lakhs ani a. Hna hi 05/10/2018 ah thawh tan a ni. A building plinth area hi 574.875 Square metres niin building hi floor nga (5) a sak a ni a. First floor hi Agriculture leh marketing lama training leh awareness centre atan ruahman niin mihring 300 vel leng tura hisap a ni. Ground floor ah hian guest room, conference/meeting room te awmin Basement I ah hian mi 78 lenna market area bakah market office ruamhan niin Basement II ah mi 85 lenna market area niin Basement III hi motor 25 lenna parking area-a ruahman a ni. reference: AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING INAUGURATED AT LUNGLEI No.523/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 28th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana on Saturday (26th February, 2022) inaugurated Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei. The Rs. 1082.93 lakhs project is implemented under the NABARD, RIDF XXIII. Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng was the guest of honour at the inauguration. RAJYA SABHA MP PU K. VANLALVENA REPRESENTS THE PROBLEMS OF MYANMAR PEOPLE TO THE VICE PRESIDENT OF INDIA No.7795/2020-2021 Aizawl, 15th March, 2021: Rajya Sabha MP Pu K. Vanlalvena, who is currently in Delhi attending the Parliament Budget Session, today met the Vice President of India and also the Chairman of Rajya Sabha, Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu, at his residence and discussed the immense suffering being faced by those working to restore democracy in Myanmar, as well as other important needs of Mizoram. Pu Vena was accompanied by MNF Adviser Pu Rosangzuala.

They informed the Vice President that many have died and been injured at the hands of the military due to the unrest in Myanmar, many are currently imprisoned, the exact number of casualties cannot be known, and it appears the numbers will continue to rise. They also informed him that a number of Myanmar military and police personnel, unwilling to use violence against the people of Myanmar, have surrendered their weapons and fled to Mizoram along with several other civilians seeking refuge. Pointing out the need to arrange humanitarian aid for these refugees entering from Myanmar, they requested the Vice President of India to take necessary steps to end the suffering of the Myanmar people. They also expressed their view that the Central Government's policy towards Myanmar needs to be reviewed.

Pu Vena and Pu Rosangzuala also requested the Vice President to take steps to appoint a Mizo in the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), as not a single person from Mizoram has ever been a member of the UPSC since India's independence. They also represented to the Vice President that even after 35 years of attaining full statehood, it is no longer appropriate for Mizoram to remain under the AGMUT cadre in the All India Civil Service, and it is time to create a separate Mizoram Cadre. Furthermore, they requested Vice President Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu to look into setting up an exam centre in Aizawl so that job aspirants under the Staff Selection Commission would no longer have to travel to Guwahati to write their exams.

hypothesis: LUNGLEI DISTRICT - COVID-19 NO TOLERANCE FORTNIGHT No.6374/2020-2021 The Covid-19 'No Tolerance Fortnight', planned by the Government of Mizoram to break the chain of the rapidly spreading Covid-19 pandemic and to help the public adopt Covid-19 restrictions as a way of life, is being strictly implemented in Lunglei District from October 26 to November 9, 2020. Along with this, the Jan Andolan Campaign, an awareness campaign for safety regarding Covid-19, is also being carried out. Yesterday, a meeting was held in the office chamber of Lunglei DC & DLTF Chairman Pu V. Lalsangliana to discuss in detail the implementation of the Covid-19 No Tolerance Fortnight in Lunglei District. During the No Tolerance Fortnight, 30 percent of staff from each government department appointed for Covid-19 Executive Duty have been divided into 24 teams, and their duty schedules have been finalized. Each team has a Team Leader who will widely sensitize the public on Covid-19 prevention guidelines and fine those who violate the guidelines without any leniency. These Covid-19 Executive Duties strictly enforce the guidelines laid down for the public under The Mizoram (Containment and Prevention of Spread of Covid-19) Act, 2020, and government orders, imposing penalties on violators and making them pay the fixed fine amount with proper challans. Starting today, in collaboration with the VLTFs of every locality, Covid-19 Executive Duty has commenced within Lunglei District. During this Covid-19 No Tolerance Fortnight, a Talkshow will be organized through Local Cable to remind the public of various information regarding the Covid-19 pandemic. Banners on Covid-19 prevention have also been put up in busy areas of Lunglei town. VLTFs have also been requested to make public announcements regarding Covid-19 prevention and guidelines three (3) times daily in various localities/villages. Attachment Loading attachment...

hypothesis: In the entire world, there is at least one whom God chose, who could say, "The ruler of the world is coming, and he has nothing in me" (John 14:30). In other words, there is not a single trace of the ruler of this world in the Lord Jesus. What we must carefully note is that when the Lord Jesus came into this world, He did not come to be God, but He came to be a man. God needed a man. If God Himself were to deal with Satan, it would have been very easy; Satan would have fallen in an instant. But God did not intend to do it Himself. He wanted a man to deal with Satan; He intended for a creature to deal with a creature. When the Lord Jesus became a man, He suffered temptation just like a man, and He experienced everything that a man experiences. This man overcame; this man is the victor. He ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of God. Jesus was crowned with "glory and honor" (Heb. 2:9), and He has been glorified.

hypothesis: If we want to know clearly the state of life in believers, we cannot look at it through the things manifested outwardly; we must know the scent and the source of what is manifested. The Centre has put an estimated amount of ₹ 1,615.00 crore for 2022-23 as recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission which is 9.78% lower than the current year’s BE.The recommended Revenue Deficit Grants diminish towards the end of the Finance Commission award period with only ₹ 586.00 crore recommended for 2025-26.

source: MIZORAM CHIEF SECRETARY HOVIN INTEGRITY PLEDGE THUTIAM CHHAM RUAL 2547/2023-2024 Vawiin ni 30th October atanga 5th November, 2023 chhungin India rampumah Vigilance Awareness Week, 2023 hman a ni dawn a. Kumin Vigilance Week thupui chu - 'Hlemhletna hnawl la, ram tan thawk rawh' (Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation) a ni. Ram hmundangte rualin vawiin chawhma khan Mizoramah pawh 'Vigilance Week 2023' hawn nan Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma kaihhruaina hnuaiah Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO-a sorkar hnathawk, officials and staff zawng zawngten a huhovin 'Integrity Pledge' thuchham an chham rual a. Sorkar office tina Heads of Office-te pawhin an hnuaia thawk officer leh staff-te nen anmahni office hmun theuhah 'Integrity Pledge' hi an chhamrual bawk a ni. He Integrity Pledge hmang hian sorkar hnathawk tupawhin hlemhletna a do tlat tur thu te, sorkar dan leh thupek anga dik leh felfai taka hnathawh a tum tur thu te, mipui rawngbawlna a ni tih hriain a nungchang leh hnathawh danah te mawihnai tak leh midangte entawn tlaka awm turin leh hlemhletna thil a hmuh emaw hriat te chu ngawih bosan mai lova, sorkarah report ngei turin thuchham an chham a ni. reference: MIZORAM CHIEF SECRETARY LEADS GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES IN TAKING INTEGRITY PLEDGE 275/2023-2024 Vigilance Awareness Week, 2023 is to be observed in the whole of India from today, i.e. 30th October till 5th November, 2023. This year the theme is - 'Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation'. Starting off the Vigilance Week in Mizoram too, Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma led the officials and staff of the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO this morning in taking the 'Integrity Pledge' in the Secretariat Courtyard. Likewise, all Heads of Offices under the State Government also led the employees in their respective offices in taking the Integrity Pledge, in which each government servant avowed to follow probity and rule of law in all walks of life, to neither take nor offer bribe, to perform all tasks in an honest and transparent manner, to act in public interest, to lead by example exhibiting integrity in personal behavior and to report any incident of corruption to the appropriate agency. Along with the rest of the country, to mark the commencement of 'Vigilance Week 2023' in Mizoram, all government officials and staff at the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO, led by Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma, collectively took the 'Integrity Pledge' this morning. Heads of Offices in every government office also administered the 'Integrity Pledge' to the officers and staff working under them at their respective offices. Through this Integrity Pledge, every government employee pledged to firmly fight against corruption, to strive to work honestly and transparently in accordance with government rules and regulations, to be polite and exemplary in their conduct and work knowing that it is a service to the public, and to report any instances of corruption they see or hear to the government instead of keeping silent. Lalthangliana, Minister, Health & Family Welfare Department, Higher & Technical Education, Commerce & Industries chuan Mobile Medical Van, Essential Drugs & Diagnostic Kits & Laptops and Speaker Mamit District Hospital, PHC/CHC leh Sub- Centre-a hman tur vailiam. Khuallian Dr. R Lalthangliana chuan Mamit District chhunga cheng te'n hriselna kawnga hma an sawn theihna tura hmanraw tangkai tak taka thuam an ni chu a lawmawm thusawiin District - 11 zinga Medical Doctor ngei District Bawrhsap, hriselna kawnga a ngaihna hria in nei chu in vannei takzet a. Aspirational District atangin Mizoram District 11- te zingah pakhatna ni thei tura tan la tura chahin in tum tlat chuan theihloh a awm lo a ni tiin kum zabi 21-a hmasawnna chu hmang tangkaiin dik taka kan hmachhawn chuan District hnufual ber thin kha a ropui ber kan ni thei a ni a ti. Dr. Thangtea chuan Pathian ringtu mizo nih hi a nuama, pi leh pute atanga lungrual tak leh inpumkhatna nena thawkho thin kan nihna chuan rah tha chhuah zelin, Covid - 19 avanga nunna chan kan nei erawh pawi hle rualin hri dona kawnga kan hmalakna-a hlawhtlinna kan hmuh mekte leh India hmarchhak State pariat (8) zingah Covid - 19 vanga thi tlemna ber State kan ni chu Pathian avang leh kan thawhhona avang a ni a ti. Minister chuan hmasawnna kan hmuh mekte chu chho zawnga thlira in delhbeh tir mai lovin hmasawnna tluantling nei turin kan tih ve theih tawk theuha tan la thar turin kalkhawmte a fuih a. Kawngpui tha nei turin hmalakna kalpui mek niin khawchhak lam atanga khawthlang lam hawiin kawngsial hna thawh tan mek a nih thu a sawi bawk. Er. H. Lalzirliana, Bialtu MLA pawhin Mamit District-in hriselna kawnga hma kan sawn theihna tur leh Aspirational District kan nihna atanga khaichhuah kan nihna tura CSR hnuai atanga hmanraw tangkai tak tak lei a ni chu lawmawm a tih thusawiin Kan District Bawrhsap-in hemi kawnga hma a lakna chu fakawm a tih thu a sawi a. Covid-19 hripuiin khawvel a tih buai mek karah Mizoram chu Sorkar hmalakna chak tak a vang te, Kohhran mite tawngtaina vang te leh khawtlang hruaitute hmalakna avangin India ram state zingah a titha ber pawl kan ni chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi bawk. Bialtu MLA chuan Mamit District-in kawngpui tha kan neih chu Mizoram Sawrkarin a ngaihpawimawh berte zing a mi a nih avangin chak taka hmalakna kalpui a ni a, hun reilote-ah kawngpui tha kan nei thuai a beisei thu a sawi. Mamit District-in hriselna lama hma kan sawna, nu naupai te'n enkawlna tha zawk an dawn a, damdawi an mamawh angte an hmuh theihna tur bakah damlote enkawlna tha zawk leh rang zawk pek an nih theihna tura District chhung PHC/CHC leh Health Sub- Centre-te tana hmanraw lei hi Mamit District Bawrhsap hmalakna-in REC LTD, CSR Health Project hnuai atanga lei a ni. Vawiin-a sem tak Bolero Camper(4WD BS6) 11 lei nan hian Rs. 1,04,50,000/- hman niin Motor-te hi Health Care delivery a bik takin vaccination drive, Health camp conduct leh awareness pekna tur bakah, kawng that lohna hmun, motor naran in a thlen theih lohna khuate awlsam taka thlen theihnan 4 wheeled drive lei a ni a. Rs. 15,60,000/- senga lei damdawi chi hrang hrang 76 - Folic Acid, Oral rehydration salt, Ibuprofen, Ascorbic Acid (vitamin C), Albendazole, Paracetamol leh Diagnostic Kits 50 - Sahli's Haemoglobinometer, Pregnancy Test Kit, Malaria Test Kit, Typhoid Test Kit, BP Instrument Mercurial, Adult Weighing Machine, Hepatitis B-Test Kit leh a dangte Sub Centre/Health & Wellness Centre- te hman tur khuallian hian a hlan bawk. He Project hian a tum ber chu Health & welness Centre hi mi tam zawkin health care services an dawn theihna tur leh a tlawhtute mamawh damdawi leh diagnostic kit te a thlawna pek chhuah a ni a, health and welness centre hi mi tam zawkin hmang tangkaia, an tlawh tam (footfall) nana kalpui a ni. Vawiin vek hian Rs. 24,60,000/- senga lei Laptop leh Speaker 52, Mamit District chhung khua tlawh pawh harsa leh health care facility nei thalo khuate tan awlsam zawka health care provider te an biak pawh zung zung theihna turin Telemedicine atan Health Department hnenah hlan a ni bawk. He hun hi Dr. Lalrozama, IAS, Deputy Commissioner chuan kaihruaiin, Pu Beitlotha Nohro, SDC pawhin report pe-in Health Project hnuaiah Aspirational District kan nih avanga hriselna lama hma kan sawn theihna tura thuam kan nih dante a tarlang a. hypothesis: HEALTH MINISTER FLAGS OFF MOBILE MEDICAL VAN AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR USE IN MAMIT DISTRICT No.7589/2020-2021 Today, Dr. R. Lalthangliana, Minister, Health & Family Welfare Department, Higher & Technical Education, Commerce & Industries flagged off Mobile Medical Vans, Essential Drugs & Diagnostic Kits, Laptops and Speakers to be used in Mamit District Hospital, PHCs/CHCs and Sub-Centres. The Chief Guest, Dr. R. Lalthangliana, expressed his happiness over the provision of these highly useful equipment to improve the health sector for the residents of Mamit District. He remarked that among the 11 districts, they are extremely fortunate to have a District Deputy Commissioner who is a medical doctor and understands the needs of the health sector. Encouraging them to strive to become the first among the 11 districts of Mizoram from being an Aspirational District, he said that if there is strong determination, nothing is impossible. He added that by utilizing 21st-century developments and facing challenges with integrity, the district which used to be the most backward can become the most outstanding. Dr. Thangtea stated that it is a joy to be a Mizo who believes in God, and our nature of working together in harmony and unity since the time of our ancestors continues to bear good fruit. While expressing deep regret over the loss of lives due to Covid-19, he said that the success we are currently seeing in our fight against the pandemic and being the state with the lowest Covid-19 mortality rate among the eight (8) North Eastern States of India is due to God and our collective cooperation. The Minister urged the gathering not to be overwhelmed by looking only at the challenges of the developments we are seeing, but to make renewed efforts in their respective capacities to achieve sustainable development. He also mentioned that initiatives are underway to construct good highways, and road construction work has begun from the east facing towards the west. Er. H. Lalzirliana, the local MLA, also expressed his gratitude for the procurement of highly useful equipment under CSR to improve the health sector in Mamit District and to uplift it from its status as an Aspirational District. He commended the District Deputy Commissioner for his initiatives in this regard. He also stated that amidst the global disruption caused by the Covid-19 pandemic, it is gratifying that Mizoram is among the best-performing states in India due to the active initiatives of the Government,

reference: HEALTH MINISTER INAUGURATES 43RD ANNUAL CONFERENCE OF IMA, MIZORAM STATE BRANCH The Indian Medical Association (IMA), Mizoram State Branch observed its 43rd annual conference today at Aijal Club where the Minister for Health and Family Welfare Department Dr.R.Lalthangliana was the Chief Guest. The theme of this yearâ€™s conference is â€œEnding the HIV&AIDS Epidemic: Community by Communityâ€. Speaking at the inaugural function, the Minister said that the government is committed to advance public health efforts and improve health for all. He encouraged the medical community to revive their efforts and recommit themselves in serving the public. Established in 1976, the Mizoram State Branch of IMA currently has 750 members out of which 33 are newly inducted. The Mizoram State Branch received two prestigious awards this year, namely the IMA Special Award for Organizing (IMA North East Leaders Meet Conclave) and President Appreciation Award (for IMA Membership Drive Trophy) from the IMA General Headquarters. The IMA is a voluntary organization where all doctors, whether employed by the government or practising in private, are registered members. The organization looks after the interest of doctors as well as the well being of the community at large. It aims to promote medical and its allied sciences, improve public health and maintain honour and dignity of the medical profession.
hypothesis:
HEALTH MINISTER ATTENDS IMA MIZORAM BRANCH CONFERENCE
Today, the Indian Medical Association (IMA) Mizoram State Branch held its 43rd Annual Conference at the Aijal Club. Dr. R. Lalthangliana, Health Minister, attended as the chief guest. The theme for this year's IMA Annual Conference was "Ending the HIV & AIDS Epidemic: Community by Community." Dr. R. Lalthangliana stated that the government prioritizes the health sector, and health is highly emphasized even in the SEDP, the main initiative of the Mizoram government. Saying that the government is open to health development and is making great efforts in building development infrastructure, the Minister stated that the government is willing to do its best for the establishment of a Cancer Super Speciality Hospital in Zemabawk, the upgrading of ZMC, the development of RIPANS, and all kinds of developments in various hospitals and healthcare within Mizoram. Dr. R. Lalthangliana said that doctors and nurses are servants of the public, performing important and honorable work. Encouraging them to continue dedicating their skills and abilities to the public, he urged them to rededicate themselves to the service they are performing, keeping in mind that beyond medical science, even their kind words alone can bring healing to patients. The opening program of the conference was chaired by IMA President Dr. Rosangliana, and Honorary Secretary Dr. Chawnglungmuana presented a report on the various activities of their association. The IMA Mizoram State Branch has 33 members and 15 new intern members. Among their existing members, there are 15 newly graduated Specialists (MD/MS). During this year, they received the IMA Special Award for Organizing (IMA North East Leaders Meet Conclave) and the President's Appreciation Award (for IMA Membership Drive Trophy) from the IMA Headquarters. This association regularly organizes Special Clinics in rural areas, where they treat patients for free using various equipment and tools. They also organize various seminars for their members to advance medical knowledge, and in this conference, they studied the issue of HIV and AIDS in detail.

reference: Did Paul disclose all his revelations? Far from it. He wrote, “I know a man [who is himself] in Christ, fourteen years ago (whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know; God knows) such a one was caught away to the third heaven” (v. 2). He did not divulge this experience until fourteen years later. What depth there was in Paul! It would be a wonder if we could hide away something we received from God for seven years. But for fourteen years Paul never divulged his experience; for fourteen years God’s church knew nothing of it; for fourteen years not one of the apostles had heard of it. Paul’s roots were deep beneath the soil.
hypothesis: Did Paul reveal everything he heard? Not at all. He wrote like this: "I know a man in Christ (referring to himself) who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of the body I do not know—God knows." (ch.2) He did not speak about this experience of his for fourteen years. How deep Paul was! If we could keep what we receive from God a secret for seven years, it would be a miracle. But for fourteen years, Paul never spoke of his experience; for fourteen years, the churches of God did not know about it at all; for fourteen years, not even one of the apostles knew about it. The roots that Paul struck deep into the earth were exceedingly deep.

reference: MYC CHAIRMAN LAYS FOUNDATION STONE FOR MYC INCUBATION CENTRE AT SERKAWN, LUNGLEI No.573/2021-2022 Aizawl the 28th March, 2022 : MYC Chairman Dr Vanlaltanpuia, Lunglei North MLA laid the foundation stone for Mizoram Youth Commission Incubation Centre at Serkawn,Lunglei near Lena Stadium on Saturday (26th March, 2022). The land for the Incubation Centre was donated by Serkawn VC. Lunglei High Powered Committee Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, Pu H. Lalnunzuala, Under Secretary MYC, Pu Lalrotluanga, President YMA Sub-Headquarters Lunglei and representatives from Serkawn locality and various NGOs were also present at the occasion. On the occasion of this foundation stone laying ceremony, MYC Chairman Dr Vanlaltanpuia said this centre would cater to the needs of aspiring Mizo youths such as competitive coaching, Information Technology, skill development and entrepreneurship. He thanked the local leaders of Serkawn who donated the property to MYC, and promised them that the centre would be used for the betterment of society and the economy. Talking about the MYC Coaching Centres in Lunglei, Siaha, Kolasib Districts and the one in Champhai which will be opened shortly, the MYC Chairman said that he along with the MYC team would continue working in earnest for the advancement of Mizo youths to the best of their capabilities. He stated that construction of MYC Youth Centres are underway at Aizawl,Serchhip and Lunglei. In addition to competitive exams, MYC is planning to continue to provide cement mistiri training, food processing training, cake baking training, cabin crew, Army Pre-Recruitment training and promotion of music and sports to help the youths reach their goals at the national level. The MYC Chairman said that the MYC Super IAS 20 which was started in 2020 will be upgraded to Super IAS 40 which will comprise of 20 more aspirants. He further said that the road connecting Khawiva, Aizawl-Thenzawl-Lunglei road and roads in Lunglei town will be repaired and that the budget for the improvement works for MZU Southern Campus is raised to Rs.15 crore. Lunglei High Powered Committee Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng shared that although the staff of MYC are few in number, their contributions to the future of Mizo youths are commendable. He stated his appreciation for the Incubation Centre and urged the people to make the most out of this centre. Pu Lalrotluanga, President YMA Sub-Headquarters Lunglei and Pu K. Zodinsanga, VCP Serkawn also gave a brief speech, Pu Lalmuanzuala, CC, MYC Lunglei ended the ceremony with vote of thanks speech. Attachment Loading attachment...

raw_text:
MYC CHAIRMAN LAYS FOUNDATION STONE FOR MYC INCUBATION CENTRE AT SERKAWN, LUNGLEI

No.4413/2021-2022
Aizawl, 26th March 2022: Today, Dr. Vanlaltanpuia, MLA of Lunglei North constituency and Chairman of the Mizoram Youth Commission (MYC), laid the foundation stone for the Mizoram Youth Commission Incubation Centre at Serkawn, Lunglei. The site for the MYC Incubation Centre is located near Lena Stadium, and the land was donated by the Serkawn Village Council (VC).

The event was attended by Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, Vice Chairman of the Lunglei High Powered Committee; Pu H. Lalnunzuala, Under Secretary of MYC; Pu Lalrotluanga, President of YMA Sub-Headquarters Lunglei; along with local leaders of Serkawn and representatives of various non-governmental organizations (NGOs).

Mizoram Youth Commission Chairman Dr. Vanlaltanpuia stated that the MYC Incubation Centre will accommodate various initiatives for youth development, including competitive coaching, Information Technology, skill development, and entrepreneurship. He also mentioned that it is planned to be a residential facility. Expressing his gratitude to the Serkawn community for generously donating their land for the future of the youth, he said that the donated land would be utilized effectively for human resource development and the growth of the state's economy.

The MYC Chairman went on to say that the MYC will continue to do its best for the development of Mizo youth. He mentioned that MYC Coaching Centres have already been opened in Lunglei, Siaha, and Kolasib Districts, and plans are underway to open one in Champhai soon. He added that MYC Youth Centres are currently under construction in Aizawl and Serchhip, and the construction of the MYC Youth Centre in Lunglei is also nearing completion.

Stating that the MYC aims to broaden the horizons of Mizo youth and guide them to meet national-level challenges, he mentioned that in addition to competitive exam coaching, initiatives such as masonry training, food processing training, cake baking training, cabin crew training, Army Pre-Recruitment training, as well as programs in music and sports are currently underway, and there are plans to expand these initiatives further.

CONVOCATION PROGRAMME HELD AT GOVT. ITI, AIZAWL

1974/2022-2023 Aizawl the 17th September, 2022: Today, for the first time in Mizoram, a Convocation Programme was held at Govt. ITI, Aizawl for 143 ITI graduates. Govt. ITI Aizawl currently has 384 students in the ongoing (2022-23) session. In the latest results, it achieved an overall pass percentage of 97.14%, which is the best result since the establishment of Govt. ITI in Mizoram. Furthermore, Govt. ITI, Aizawl secured the sixth position among various states across India. During this convocation, certificates were presented to 143 students.

In the Convocation Programme, Pu K Lalhmingliana, Director of LESDE Department, delivered the welcome address and expressed his gratitude for the success of the graduating students, which will contribute to the continuous progress of the Mizoram Skills sector. The Chief Guest, Pu Lalramsanga Sailo, Secretary of LESDE Department, stated that he was very pleased with the continuous progress of ITI education in Mizoram and the active participation of Mizo youth in skill development. He expressed pride that Govt. ITI, Aizawl emerged as one of the top performers among thousands of Govt. ITIs in India. He also added that to ensure the country's continuous development and to enable the youth to stand on their own feet through their skills, it is important to continue upgrading the ITIs.

Most of the technician-level workers in Mizoram are graduates of Govt. ITI, Aizawl. Among the ITI graduates, 14 students under the Motor Mechanic Vehicle (MMV) trade received offers of appointment from major companies even before their results were declared.

A nationwide convocation has never been held before, but under the initiative of the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE), it has been started from this year. The Convocation was held simultaneously across different parts of India, with the main event being held in Delhi under the leadership of Prime Minister Pu Narendra Modi. The Convocation is planned to be held annually on the occasion of Vishwakarma Diwas (Day).

raw_text:
FINAL ELECTORAL ROLLS RELEASED FOR USE IN THE TOKALO MDC CONSTITUENCY BY-ELECTION

Yesterday afternoon (15.10.2019) at 1:00 PM, the District Election Officer and Deputy Commissioner, Pu Bhupesh Chaudhary, IAS, released the Final Electoral Rolls to be used in the upcoming MDC By-Election for the Tokalo Constituency in his office chamber. He also handed over both hard and soft copies of the Final Electoral Rolls to representatives of various political parties. 

This By-Election is being held due to the demise of the incumbent MDC of Tokalo constituency, Pu K.L. Bana. With January 1, 2019, as the qualifying date, the Summary Revision of Electoral Rolls was successfully conducted as scheduled by the State Election Commission, and today was the designated date for the release of the Final Electoral Rolls.

The release of the Final Electoral Rolls was attended by Pu K. Vanlalthiana, Addl. DC; Pu Amol Srivastava, IAS, Asst. Commissioner; Pu H. Zonunmawia, Election Officer; Pu N. Vabeiratlua, DIPRO; representatives of non-governmental organizations MTP(H) and MCHP(H); and representatives of various political parties.

According to the released Electoral Rolls, there are 450 female voters and 505 male voters in the 1-Tokalo constituency, making a total of 955 voters.

raw_text:
SPORTS MINISTER HONORS NES U-19 TEAM
Under the auspices of Headquarters 23 Sector Assam Rifles, a 'Felicitation Programme' was organized today at Loch Hall, 46 Assam Rifles Headquarters, to honor the Mizoram Team who recently emerged champions in the NES Under-19 Women's Football Championship. The event was graced by Sports Minister Pu Robert Romawia Royte. Leaders of the Mizoram Football Association (MFA) also attended the function.

Speaking on the occasion, Sports Minister Pu Robert Romawia Royte congratulated the Mizoram Girls U-19 Team on winning the NES U-19 Championship. He stated that this victory does not belong to the Government, the organizers and facilitators Assam Rifles, or the MFA alone, but belongs to all the people of Mizoram, adding that the team is the pride of the people of Mizoram. He pointed out that the Mizoram girls' team defeating the Nagaland girls' team, who recently represented India at the international level, demonstrates how good our female footballers are. He mentioned that the Government, on its part, will continue to take steps to supplement, encourage, and strengthen the MFA's initiatives for the development of football, and he invited the MFA leaders to continue and strengthen the excellent cooperation between the Government and the MFA.

Pu Robert Romawia Royte spoke about how football is a great tool for national unity and strength, stating that through football, the Northeast states and other parts of India have become closer, creating a better atmosphere of brotherhood and strengthening national unity. He remarked that the power of football is great and cannot be underestimated. He said that as the Government wants to develop other sports disciplines even further alongside football, the Mizoram Sports Policy, which Mizoram has never had before, is currently being drafted. He added that the growth of sports disciplines like taekwondo, basketball, and volleyball is encouraging, and the Government is currently working on ways to strengthen sports associations. As the Sports Minister, he stated he would do his utmost to ensure better administration.

He also mentioned that efforts are underway to install good floodlighting at the Rajiv Gandhi Sports Stadium to enable hosting international level matches, that sites are being identified to construct about 4 to 5 more football fields in Aizawl city, that sanction has been obtained for laying turf at the Zembawk field, and that plans are also being made to lay turf at the Khawzawl field.

source: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati in Sainik School Chhingchhip a tlawh 2122/2022-2023 Chhingchhip, the 30th September 2022: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan vawiin khan Sainik School Chhingchhip a tlawh a. He hunah hian School building leh hmunhma te a endik a, Sikul naupangte hmaah fuihna thu a sawi bawk a ni. Governor hian Sainik School a thlenin amah zahna chibai 8 Bn Assam Rifles ten School kawtah an lo buk a. Wcdr Shahul Hameed, Principal leh Maj S.Kalyan, Administrative Officer ten zirtirtute leh School staff te an hmelhriattir chhunzawm a. Hemi zawh hian Principal Office ah Sainik School dinhmunte inhrilhhriatna hun neih leh a ni a. Assembly Hall-ah Official programme leh Cultural Programme neih chhunzawm nghal a ni. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan Principal leh a thawhpui ten Sainik School tha tak ni tur leh hmun danga Sainik School te dinhmun pha tura theihtawp an chhuah chu fakawm a tih thu a sawi hmasa a. Mizoram sawrkarin hetiang ang School tha bik Mizorama zirlaite tan a buatsaih thei chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi bawk a ni. Sainik School Chhingchhip hi India ram hmundang te aia a danglam bik na chu helai hmunah hian Sainik School dangte entawn turin a vawikhatna atana leh a hmahruaitu ni turin hmeichhe naupangte luh tir an ni a. Hei hi a chhuanawm tak zet a ni a ti. Sainik School te hi khawi hmunah pawh School thabik an ni a, Sipai, Navy leh Airforce Officer ni turin a bik takin heng schoolah te hian zirlai te zirtirna pek a ni a ti. Sainik School a zirlaite hi Armed Forces ah an thawkvek kher lo a nih pawhin khawtlang leh ram tana khua leh tui entawn tlak ni tura chher an nih thu a sawi bawk. India chakna chu danglamna tam tak kara inpumkhatna leh inunauna tha a ni tih zirlaite chu a hrilh nawn leh a. He mawhphurhna huangah hian Sainik School zirlaite chu hmahruaitu ni turin a chah a ni. Full speech of the Honble Governor : dipr.mizoram.gov.in/post/speech-of-dr-hari-babu-kambhampati-honble-governor-of-mizoram-on-the-occasion-of-visit-to-sainik-school-chhingchhip-on-30th-september-2022 Maj S.Kalyan, Adm in Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati lawmna thu a sawi hmasa a. Hemi hnu hian Assembly Hall chhunga programme hi tan a ni a. Zirlai ten Governor pualin Cultural programme an hmang a. WCdr Shahul Hameed, Principal, Sainik School, Chhingchhip chuan lawmthu sawiin huntawp a khar a ni. Official programme zawh hian Saini School Campus chhunga School building leh hmunhma te Governor chuan a endik chhunzawm nghal a ni. Principal Report atanga a lan dan chuan Sainik School Chhingchhip hi kum 6 hmel a hmu mek a. Tunah hian batch hmasa ber(Class VI) te chu Class XI an ni mek a ni. Sainik School a lut tur hian All India Entrance Test paltlang a ngai a. Sikul naupang pakhat tana kum khat chhunga senso chu Rs 1.85 lakh velah chhut a ni. Kumtin Class VI ah hian mipa naupang 60 leh Hmeichhe naupang 10 admission pek an ni mek a. Class IX ah erawh chuan mipa chiah admission pek niin kum tin seat 10 a awm thin a ni. School naupangte hian zing dar 5 vel atangin zan dar 9:30 vel thleng nitin, lehkha zirna hun, infiamna leh thildang tangkai zir nan hun an hmang thin a. Lehkha zirna leh a kaihhnaih(cocurricular activities) bakah zirlaite tan hian taksa insawizawina leh themthiamna chidangte ( extracurricular activities) atana hmunhma pawimawh Football Ground, Badminton Court, Basketball Court, Gynasium, Music room,etc., te he school hian a nei a. Swimming pool, parade ground leh sports facility tangkai tak tak buatsaih chhoh zel a tum bawk. Principal hian Mizoram sawrkar in tanpuina a pek thin - GIA dinhmun te, Ambulance te chi MRB in CSR kaltlanga pek a tum chungchang te, NCC te tana tangkai INSAS silai Home Department, Govt of Mizoram in pek a tum chunchang te Rs 99,96,000 school tihphuisuina atana Ministry of Defence atang sum lo kal tur chungchangte a sawi a. An harsatna pahnih Tui Bill sang tak leh Electric chhit man sang lutuk chungchangte pawh sawi a ni. Kawlphetha a harsatna sutkian a nih theih nan campus chhunga Solar Power Generation Plant bun turin Governor chuan Sainik School Chhingchhip hotute chu thurawn a pe a. Tui bill chungchang pawh Serchhip DC office leh PHED ten chinfel sak turin hma an la mek tih sawi a ni. Governor in Sainik School, Chhingchhip a tlawhnaah hian Pu Lalmuansanga Ralte, Addl DC leh Pu Stephen Lalrinawma, SP, Serchhip District pawh an tel a ni. Attachment Loading attachment...
reference: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visits Sainik School Chhingchhip 191/2022-2023 Chhingchhip, the 30th September 2022: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati who is on an official tour of Serchhip District visited Sainik School, Chhingchhip, a few miles away from Serchhip town today. Upon his arrival, Governor was accorded the Guard of Honour by 8 Bn of Assam Rifles. He was then introduced to the staff by Wcdr Shahul Hameed, Principal, and Maj S.Kalyan, Administrative Officer. A briefing about the School to Governor was given by the Principal in his office room. After this, an official function with a cultural program was organized inside the Assembly Hall in honour of the esteemed visitor. Here, the Governor addressed the students. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati congratulated faculties for their best effort to keep up with other establishwd Sainik Schools in the country. He thanked the state government for bring up a highly valuable asset of national importance in education like Sainik school here in Mizoram. He expressed his pride of having the first Sainik School in the country where girl students are admitted. He stressed the importance of Sainik Schools for preparing the young students to become cadet officers in Army, Airforces and Navy. Beside this, he said the school also prepared the students to become role model students and role model citizen. He reminded the students of the school about their important duties for the national integration of the county. Full speech of the Honble Governor : https://dipr.mizoram.gov.in/post/speech-of-dr-hari-babu-kambhampati-honble-governor-of-mizoram-on-the-occasion-of-visit-to-sainik-school-chhingchhip-on-30th-september-2022 The programme began with welcome address by Maj S.Kalyan, Admn and concluded with vote of thanks proposed by WCdr Shahul Hameed, Principal, Sainik School, Chhingchhip. After the official programme, Governor inspected the facilities inside the campus of Sainik School Chhingchhip. As per the briefing by the Principal, here are the few highlights of the school. The school is now 6 years old and running with the pilot cadets in Class XI. The annual intake of students are 60 boys and 10 girls in the class VI while in the class IX only boys are admitted with the availability of 10 seats for students annually. The annual fee per a student is estimated at Rs 1.85 lakh per year. The schools have daily routine for winter and summer and winter with the physical and classroom activities through out the day. It usually starts from very early morning till 9:00 to 9:30 PM at night. Apart from the facilities for cocurricular activities, the School is also currently having the facilities like Football Ground, Badminton Court, Basketball Court, Gynasium, Music room,etc.,. The swimming pool, parade ground and other big sports facilities are being planned to be added very soon. The Principal highlighted the status of Grant in Aid from the state, issues with water and power bills, LMV ambulance to be received from the Mizoram Rural Bank through CSR, INSAS rifles to be received from Home Department, Government of Mizoram, Infrastructural Fund received to the tune of Rs 99,96,000 the Ministry of Defence with the proposed implementations. To solve the issue with high power bills, the Governor advised implementation of Solar Power Generation plant inside the campus. While, the issue with high water bills is being taken up the office Deputy Commissioner and is expected to be solved very soon. Governor in his visit to Sainik School, Chhingchhip was escorted and given a company by Pu Lalmuansanga Ralte, Addl DC and Pu Stephen Lalrinawma, SP, Serchhip District. hypothesis: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visits Sainik School Chhingchhip 2122/2022-2023 Chhingchhip, the 30th September 2022: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visited Sainik School Chhingchhip today. During this visit, he inspected the school buildings and infrastructure, and also delivered an encouraging speech to the school students. Upon his arrival at Sainik School, the Governor was presented a guard of honour by the 8 Bn Assam Rifles at the school courtyard. Wcdr Shahul Hameed, Principal, and Maj S. Kalyan, Administrative Officer, then introduced the teachers and school staff to him. Following this, a briefing session on the status of Sainik School was held in the Principal's Office. The official programme and cultural programme then commenced in the Assembly Hall. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati first expressed his appreciation for the efforts made by the Principal and his colleagues to make Sainik School an excellent institution and to match the standards of Sainik Schools in other regions. He also expressed his gratitude that the Government of Mizoram could establish such a special school for the students of Mizoram. He stated that Sainik School Chhingchhip is unique compared to other parts of India because, for the first time and as a pioneer for other Sainik Schools to emulate, girls have been admitted here. He remarked that this is truly commendable. He added that Sainik Schools are premier schools everywhere, and students in these schools are specially trained to become officers in the Army, Navy, and Air Force. He also mentioned that even if the students of Sainik School do not all serve in the Armed Forces, they are molded to become exemplary citizens for the society and the nation. He reminded the students that India's strength lies in unity and brotherhood amidst great diversity. In this sphere of responsibility, he urged the Sainik School students to be leaders. source: Presbyterian Communications Board/Department hna pui ber chu thu ziak rawngbâwlnain hma a sâwn zêl theih nân, Synod leh a hnuaia pêng hrang hrangten thil chhut tûr an neih apiang fel taka chhut te, chûng zînga zawrh chi chu mipuiin an lei theih tûra a tlâwm thei anga zawrh a ni. Synod hnuaia Department hrang hrangten lehkhabu leh thil dang chhut ngai an neihte chu Synod Press-a chhut zêl tûra tih a ni a (SEC 233:39). Chutiang bawkin Synod Office leh a hnuaia Department hrang hrangten office mamawh (stationeries) an neihte chu a theih hrâm chuan Synod Bookroom-a mi lei tûra tih a ni a, Synod Bookroom-in an pêk theih loh thu an ziak thilte chauh hmun danga lei tûra tih a ni {Synod Sum Vawn Dân Bung 10:10 (1)}.
reference: The main objectives of the Presbyterian Communication Board/Department is to spread the Gospel through publication and printing words and it is responsible for the publication of any works required by Synod and all the departments under it. It also provides cheaper and accessible books for the masses as well. Synod and its departments are to publish their books and any other publication under Synod Press. (SEC 233:39). Similarly, all the departments are to buy their stationary needs from the Synod Bookroom as well. {Synod Sum VawnDân Bung 10:10 (1)}.
hypothesis: The main work of the Presbyterian Communications Board/Department is to ensure that the literature ministry continues to progress, to properly print whatever printing materials the Synod and its various departments have, and to sell those intended for sale at the lowest possible price so that the public can purchase them. It is directed that books and other printing requirements of the various departments under the Synod should always be printed at the Synod Press (SEC 233:39). Similarly, the Synod Office and its various departments are directed to purchase their office requirements (stationeries) from the Synod Bookroom as far as possible, and they are permitted to purchase from other places only those items which the Synod Bookroom has certified in writing that they cannot provide {Synod Financial Rules Chapter 10:10 (1)}.

source: ASSAM RIFLES BATTALION-IN ROZGAR MELA BUATSAIH DAWN 1663/2023-2024 Aizawl, the 26th August, 2023: Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (East) hnuaia Assam Rifles Battalion chuan August ni 28, 2023 hian Rozgar Mela/Job Fair tum 8-na 2 AR Gajraj Hall, Lakhimpur Battalion, Aizawl-ah a buatsaih dawn. Sawrkar laipui ruahmannain Rozgar Mela/Job Fair chu August ni 28, Thawhtanni hian State hrang hrang 25 a hmun 44 ahte huaihawt a ni dawn a. He hunah hian Indian Government hnuai Department hrang hranga hna hmu thar mi 70,000 dawnte hnenah appointment letter pek chhuah a ni ang. Prime Minister Pu Narendra Modi chuan ram pum huap hun hman hi a kaihruai dawn a, live streaming kaltlangin thalaite hnena thuchah a sawi hnuah hna hmu thar a hmuna awmte hnenah appointment letter a sem chhuak dawn a ni. Mizorama Rozgar Mela/Job Fair hlawhtling taka huaihawt a nih theih nan Assam Rifles chuan hma a la a, he hun hi Sawrkar laipuia Minister of State for Minority Affairs Pu John Barla chuan a hmanpui dawn a, hna hmu tharte kutah appointment letter a hlan dawn a ni. Ram chhung hmun hrang hranga hun hmante hi Prime Minister chuan Video Conferencing kaltlangin a chhim dawn a ni. Rozgar Mela hi Sawrkar laipuiin hna neilote tana hna a siam sakna kawnga hmalakna ngaih pawimawh tak a ni.
reference: ASSAM RIFLES BATTALION TO CONDUCT 8TH ROZGAR MELA FOR MIZORAM STATE 195/2023-2024 Aizawl the 26th August, 2023 - Battalion of Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (East) will be conducting 8th Rozgar Mela on 28 August 2023 at 2 AR Gajraj Hall, Lakhimpur Battalion. A large number of individuals will be benefitted by the Mela. Central Government is set to organize the 8th Job Fair on 28 August 2023. Notably, our Honorable Prime Minister Narendra Modi will preside over the event, addressing the youth through live streaming, followed by the distribution of appointment letter to the candidates present. Assam Rifles is playing a pivotal role in organizing the Rozgar Mela for the state of Mizoram and overseeing the eventâ€™s coordination. The Honorable Minister of Minority Affairs, Mr John Barla will personally hand over appointment letter to the candidates. The Rozgar Mela is a step towards fulfillment of the duty of Government to accord highest priority to employment generation.

reference: Let me also state that people must not rush to push the government to provide for their needs. So, time management is the most important key. I think the way files are processed hierarchy-wise also needs to be revised to save more time.
hypothesis: And, Mr. Speaker, we will not be able to mention all the grand initiatives and plans that the government has put forward. raw_text:
HPC VICE CHAIRMAN PRESIDES OVER HONOURING OF MIZORAM STATE GAMES MEDALISTS
Today, at the Lunglei BDO Conference Hall, a ceremony was held to honour the medalists from Lunglei East Assembly Constituency in the Mizoram State Games 2019, which concluded last December. The event was presided over by Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, MLA of Lunglei East AC and Vice Chairman of Lunglei HPC.

In the Mizoram State Games 2019, Lunglei East AC won 23 medals (Gold – 7, Silver – 7, Bronze - 9) across various sports disciplines, ranking 11th in the whole of Mizoram and first within Lunglei District.

Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng expressed his delight at Lunglei East AC achieving such a good position in the Mizoram State Games 2019, stating that it was the result of the hard work and dedication of the Organizing Committee members, athletes, and party leaders, and thanked them all. Encouraging the athletes to put in their best efforts to achieve success not only at the State Level but also at the National and International Levels, he urged them to continue guiding their fellow youths in a positive direction and emphasized the importance of education in whatever path they choose. He also advised them to look into and study the welfare schemes planned by the government for athletes.

Those honoured today were medalists from various sports disciplines, who were presented with appreciation certificates and cash prizes. Lunglei East AC participated in 19 out of the 32 sports disciplines in the Mizoram State Games, winning 23 medals (Gold – 7, Silver – 7, Bronze - 9) to rank 11th in the whole of Mizoram and first in Lunglei District.

Bronze Medal – Citation + Rs. 2000/-

raw_text:
CLEANLINESS WEEK 2021 CONCLUDED IN CHAMPHAI

No.2543/2021-2022

Aizawl, the 8th October, 2021: Cleanliness Week 2021, observed from October 2 to October 8 under the theme 'Cleanliness - From our homes and surroundings', was concluded today at 2:00 PM at the Horticulture Complex, New Champhai.

District Deputy Commissioner Pi Maria C.T. Zuali graced the event as the chief guest and distributed prizes to the selected winners of various cleanliness competitions.

Chief Guest Pi Maria C.T. Zuali stated that cleanliness initiatives should not end with the conclusion of the week but must be practiced throughout the year. "Every individual has an equal responsibility to make Champhai District cleaner," she said, adding that if every household dedicates at least one hour daily towards cleanliness, it can become the cleanest district. She urged the residents of the district to make every effort to keep Champhai District clean and preserved, highlighting its pleasant climate, beautiful and lush green environment, scenic wet rice cultivation fields, and other beautiful spots that other places do not have.

Emphasizing that the residents themselves are the most important factor in preserving the beauty and pleasantness of Champhai, she said that since we ourselves are often the ones who litter, we must not throw garbage carelessly when visiting beautiful and pleasant spots in the town and its surroundings. She also mentioned plans to install dustbins in all important places and tourist spots, adding, "If we actively continue to educate ourselves on cleanliness in schools, organizations, communities, offices, and churches, we will be able to make rapid progress."

Prizes for various competitions held in connection with Cleanliness Week were distributed during the function. The detailed results of the competitions in various categories are as follows:

CHIEF MINISTER ATTENDS GRADUATION AND LAMP LIGHTING CEREMONY AT RIPANS

Today, Chief Minister Pu Zoramthanga attended the graduation ceremony for students who successfully completed various Nursing and Paramedical courses this year, as well as the Lamp Lighting Ceremony to welcome 35 new Bachelor of Nursing students at the Regional Institute of Paramedical and Nursing Sciences (RIPANS) as the Chief Guest. He also presented the Proficiency Award to outstanding students.

The Chief Minister congratulated the new graduates. Stating that using one's knowledge to care for and heal fellow human beings is a noble profession, he wished the passing-out students success, encouraging them to continue working with diligence and sincerity in their future endeavors.

The Chief Minister stated that the government prioritizes the improvement of human health and better healthcare services in Mizoram. He added that the government alone cannot achieve this, and public support is essential if the country is to truly progress in terms of health. The Chief Minister expressed his happiness over the ongoing initiatives to upgrade RIPANS and assured that he would do his best to assist with the difficulties they face due to staff shortages.

The Chief Minister also presented the RIPANS Proficiency Award to the top performers in each department among the new graduates.

During today's function, RIPANS Director Dr. Chawngthanliana and Lamp Lighter Civil Hospital Nursing Superintendent Pi Lalrinthangi also delivered speeches. There are 35 students in the first year of B.Sc Nursing today. RIPANS Director Dr. Chawngthanliana presented Certificates of Appreciation to the new Graduate and Post Graduate students.

A total of 180 students graduated this year. They are:
i) B.Sc. Nursing - 36
ii) B.Sc. MLT (Medical Laboratory Technology) - 40
iii) B. Pharm - 23
iv) B. Optometry - 34
v) B.Sc. RIT (Radio Imaging Technology) - 31
vi) M. Pharm - 16

RIPANS was established in 1996 by the North Eastern Council (NEC) for the people of Northeast India to study Paramedical and Health Sciences, and from April 2007, it was placed under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare of the Central Government. source: GOVERNOR PU HARI BABU KAMBHAMPATI IN CHAMPHAI WINERY TLAWH, PMUY LEH PMAY-HFA URBAN HAMTHATNA DAWNGTUTE TLAWHIN A KAWM 3449/2022-2023 Champhai, the 1st February, 2023: Ni hnih cham tura Champhai tlawha thang mek Mizoram Governor Pu Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan vawiin chawhnu khan Champhai Winery, Tlangsam tlawhin an hmalaknate a enfiah a; Champhal Grape Growers Society leh Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Limited hotute a kawm bawk. Hemi hnu hian Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) leh Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Housing for All (Urban) hnuaia hamthatna dawngtute tlawhin a kawm a ni. Governor hi Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister Pu T.J. Lalnuntluanga, Champhai South bialtu MLA ni bawk bakah DC Champhai Pu James Lalrinchhana, SP Pu Lalrinpuia Varte leh Official dangten an tawiawm a ni. Governor Pu Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan Champhai Winery tlawh theia a awm chu lawmawm a tih thu sawiin, an hmalaknate engemawchen a lo hriat tawh thu a sawi a. Champhai District-a Winery pahnih lai a awm leh loneitute intelkhawmin an kalpui chu ropui a tih thu a sawi a. Grape chingtuten harsatna an tawh chu pawi a tih thu sawiin, Sawrkarin dan thar siama hma a la chu lawmawm a ti a. Wine siam chu food processing hnuaia a awm anih thu sawiin, agriculture product-te cheibawla siam danglam value addition chu hmalakna pawimawh tak a ni, a ti a. Tun aia nasaa huang zauh leh changtlung zawka kal tura Ministry of Food Processing Industries kaltlanga hmalakna an nei chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi bawk. Governor chuan Grape chauh nilo thei dang sawr leh um theihte pawh ngaihvena huang zauh a tul thu a sawi a. An hmalak lehzelna turah duhsakna a hlan a, Mizoram mai nilo India rama loneitute tana entawntlak leh tihhmuhtu nih tum turin a chah a ni. Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister Pu T.J. Lalnuntluanga chuan Champhai District chhunga loneitute hmalakna pawimawh tak grape sawngbawlna hmunhma Governor-in a hun hlu tak senga a tlawh chu lawmawm a ti a. Hun harsa tak paltlanga dan anga grape zawrhna tur dan thar Sawrkarin a siam thu sawiin, grape chingtuten hmabak eng tak an neih thu sawiin duhsakna a hlan a. Tun aia nasa zawka hma la a, ram ngaw humhalh nan kum tina lovah thin bansana lo nghet nei thei tura ngaihtuahna seng turin a chah a. Tun atanga reiloteah Sapthei sawngbawlna turte pawh buaipui tum anih thu sawiin, harsatna an neihte a hnena thlen hrehlo turin a chah a ni. Inkawmhona hun Packing Hall, Champhai Winery, Tlangsama hman hi Pu HS.Vanlalfakzuala, Chairman, Champhai Grape Growers Society (CGGS) chuan a kaihruai a. Pu Hrilchunglura, General Manager hnen atangin report ngaihthlak a ni a. Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Limited hotute atangin thusawi ngaihthlak a ni bawk. Mizoram hi North East India-a grape thar awm chhun leh India rama grape thar tam 5-na niin, Champhai leh Hnahlan-ah Winery a awm a. CGGS enkawl Champhai Winery hian kum 14 hmel a hmu tawh a, an Grape sawngbawl hi Bangalore Blue variety niin, vawiin thlengin Grape quintal ,15,218 an lei tling tawh a, hemi atan hian Rs 5,78,41,160/- (cheng vaibelchhe nga maktaduai sarih nuai riat singli sangkhat za leh sawmruk) an seng tawh a ni. Kum 2010 atang khan Grape quintal 918 leiin bul an tan a, kum kalta khan quintal 1144.98 an lei tling a, an Grape lakte hi herin a umna zemah an um mek a ni. Kum 2007 khan Champhai Grape Growers Association (CGGA) tih thin chu Winery din anih dawn avangin Champhai Grape Growers Society (CGGS) ti a thlak niin, Firms & Society-ah an inziahlut a ni. MIP sum cheng nuai 83 (loan) hmanga bultan niin, he loan hi November ni 9, 2020 khan Sawrkar chuan rulh let ngai lo turin grant-ah a leh sak a ni. Champhai Grape Growers Society-ah hian Governing Board Member 15 awmin kum 2 danah inthlan thin a ni a. Tun dinhmunah hian Champhai Grape Growers Society-ah hian Grape chingtu member 134 awm mekin, Staff leh Worker mi 30, Executive Member 9 leh Office Bearer 6 an awm mek bawk a. Champhai Grape Growers Society hnuaiah hian Branch 9 awm mekin mumal taka inenkawlna kalpui thin a ni. CGGS hian Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MOFPI) kaltlangin project an kalpui mek a. DC Office kaltlangin Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) hnuaiah Commerce & Industries Department hnuaiah project dil mek a ni bawk a. Dan thar hnuaiah Winery License an nei fel tawh a, State pawn thlenga hralhchhuak thei turin hmachhawp an nei a ni. Champhai Winery a tlawh zawh hian Governor chuan BPL family-te tana a thlawna eirawngbawlna gas connection pekna scheme, Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) kaltlanga hamthatna dawngtu leh khawpuia cheng insak tanpuina scheme, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Housing for All (Urban) dawngtu Tlangsam ami te a tlawh a; scheme awmzia leh tangkainate a sawifiah a, an hmuh dan leh chhawr tangkai dante a zawt nghal bawk. reference: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visits Champhai Tlangsam Winery 326/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 1st February 2023 : Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati, who is on a two-day tour of Champhai District visited the Tlangsam Winery on the outskirt of Champhai Town this evening. At the site, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati was given an escorted tour to various units by the managing officers of the winery. Thereafter, a short program was held at B Remmawia Packing hall, Champhai Winery. Governor Hari Babu expressed his delight in visiting the factory started, owned, and managed by a society of farmers. He was particularly appreciative of having witness the production centre where the determined farmers themselves added value to their products. He congratulated the Champhai Grape Growers Society and the Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Ltd. Governor welcomed the ambitious proposal to upgrade these wineries at Champhai and Hnahlan to accomodate the growing production of the Grapes in these areas. He extended his support for this proposal and if necessary, he agreed to discuss the matter with the authorities in the Ministry of Food Processing Industries(MoFPI). On behalf of Champhai Winery, Pu Hrilchunglura, General Manager, Champhai Grape Growers Society(GGGS) gave a report. The Winery was started in 2007. After 14 years of existence with the production actually started in 2010 the Winery has now grown. At present the society has 134 members. The fruit is of Bangalore Blue variety. During last year the Winery bought 1144.98 qts of grapes. As the grape production increases, CGGS submitted two projects - one project to MoFPI and another project to state department under Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK). Expressing his sympathy for the difficulties faced by grape growers, he welcomed the government's initiative in enacting new regulations. He noted that wine-making falls under food processing, and emphasized that value addition through processing agricultural products is a very important step. He also expressed his appreciation for the initiatives being undertaken through the Ministry of Food Processing Industries to expand and strengthen the operations on a larger scale than before. hypothesis: 5th STATE LEVEL TASK FORCE MEETING. Today at 11:00 AM, a meeting of the State Level Task Force (SLTF) on the National Railway Project was held at the I&PR Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Task Force Chairman Pu Zasanga, IPS (Rtd). In this meeting, Land Acquisition, Forest Clearance, the Proposal for Khanrek Railway Station, and the Construction of a Railway Station at Sihhmui were discussed. Pu V.P. Srivastava, Chief Engineer, NF Railways, Guwahati, presented a report on the work completed so far; he stated that the Final Location Survey (FLS) is still progressing smoothly, and that GPS, Traversing, and Topography Surveys between Bairabi and Sairang (51.21 Kms) have been fully completed. He also mentioned that the Final Stacking Alignment was started from Bairabi and Hortoki on April 17, 2010, and is expected to be completed before May 31, 2010. To inspect the work done by NF Railways and to ensure smoother progress regarding Land Acquisition and Forest Clearance, it was decided that a Joint Survey by three departments—Revenue, Forest, and Railways—will be conducted on April 26, 2010, under the leadership of the Kolasib Deputy Commissioner.
raw_text: 5th STATE LEVEL TASK FORCE MEETING. Today at 11:00 AM, a meeting of the State Level Task Force (SLTF) on the National Railway Project was held at the I&PR Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Task Force Chairman Pu Zasanga, IPS (Rtd). In this meeting, Land Acquisition, Forest Clearance, the Proposal for Khanrek Railway Station, and the Construction of a Railway Station at Sihhmui were discussed. Pu V.P. Srivastava, Chief Engineer, NF Railways, Guwahati, presented a report on the work completed so far; he stated that the Final Location Survey (FLS) is still progressing smoothly, and that GPS, Traversing, and Topography Surveys between Bairabi and Sairang (51.21 Kms) have been fully completed. He also mentioned that the Final Stacking Alignment was started from Bairabi and Hortoki on April 17, 2010, and is expected to be completed before May 31, 2010. To inspect the work done by NF Railways and to ensure smoother progress regarding Land Acquisition and Forest Clearance, it was decided that a Joint Survey by three departments—Revenue, Forest, and Railways—will be conducted on April 26, 2010, under the leadership of the Kolasib Deputy Commissioner.

reference: PU LAWMAWMA TOCHHAWNG VICE CHAIRMAN HPC INAUGURATES RENOVATED LUNGLEI POLICE STATION BUILDING 151/2023-2024 Lunglei;the 1st August,2023 : Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, Vice Chairman, HPC Lunglei inaugurated a newly renovated Lunglei Police Station Building(Ground Floor) here in Lunglei town, today. Lunglei PS building was constructed wayback in 1991 and the building became dilapidated and worn out.Lunglei PS building is a two storey building. Lunglei High Powered Committee Funded this renovation works, at the tune of Rs.15 lakh for each storey. Rs.15 lakh was released for the year 202-2023 which was being used for renovation of Ground Floor, which was inaugurated today. Fund for 1st Floor renovation is also released for the year 2023-2024 and renovation works will be carried out by Police dept, at their earliest. In his augural speech Pu Lawmawma highlighted that Lunglei PS managed to bag the Best Police Station of India Award during 2022-2023.It is quite befitting that the building is also renovated to become the best PS building in Mizoram. He applauded the renovation works executed by PS staff with their all out efforts and with a spirit of love and ownership to get the best result. He exhorted them, since they could manage to bag the Best PS Award too, to try for the Best in traffic management in the whole India. He implored PS staff to be friendly and polite all the time, so that the public will not have any hesitation and fear in approaching the Police station in their time of troubles and distresses. Pu H.Ramthlengliana,IPS,DIG(SR) and Pi Ramdinliani IAS, DC delivered speeches in this function as well. Pu H.Ramthlengliana,IPS,DIG(SR) informed the gathering public how HPC had helped police dept. time and again since many past years and said that renovation works was just one amongst many. He entreated and reminded the police dept. to pay back many blessings they had received from various quarters by rendering their best services to the society. Pi Ramdinliani IAS, DC Lunglei heartily congratulated PS staff for their newly renovated building and applauded them for their dedication and hard work put forth in their renovation works and added that it was worth emulating for other depts. Todayâ€™s brief inaugural function was presided over Pu K.Beihmotaosa MPS,Addl.SP Lunglei and Pu Rahool Alwal IPS, SP Lunglei delivered welcome speech,and technical report was given by Pu L.P Zohmangaiha,OC Lunglei PS. reference: SIAHA DC CONDUCTS SURPRISED VISITS TO SOME OFFICES Deputy Commissioner, Siaha District, Pu Bhupesh Chaudhary IAS, conducted a surprised visit to some of the Offices, here at Siaha, today. Pu Bhupesh said that he conducted a surprised visits not to find faults, but to know better the set-up and working-nature of each and every office under his jurisdiction, to listen to them and aware of their problems, and most of all;to remind them of the staff that dereliction of duties will be viewed seriously and DC will keep vigil over them all the time. hypothesis:
SIAHA DC PAYS SURPRISE VISIT TO SEVERAL OFFICES
The Deputy Commissioner of Siaha District, Pu Bhupesh Chaudhary, IAS, paid surprise visits to several offices this morning. Pu Bhupesh stated, "My purpose in conducting this 'surprise visit' is not to expose the shortcomings of the offices or to humiliate them, but to understand the administration of various offices and to listen to the difficulties they face. At the same time, the DC is constantly monitoring the work and functioning of the various offices under his jurisdiction, and I want it to be known that he will be very strict with staff who neglect their duties or are undisciplined." The offices he visited today were: ITI (Industrial Training Institute), Excise & Narcotics Office, Mizofed, Printing & Stationery Depot, and FCS & Consumer Affairs' Godown. It is intended to conduct these surprise visits whenever there is an opportunity, with the aim of visiting all offices and educational institutions under the Government of Mizoram. During his surprise visit today, the DC was accompanied by Pu Amol Srivastava, IAS, Asst. Commissioner, Pu H. Zonunmawia, Election Officer, and Pu N. Vabeiratlua, DIPRO.

At the same time, the DC is constantly monitoring the work and functioning of the various offices under his jurisdiction, and I want it to be known that he will be very strict with staff who neglect their duties or are undisciplined." The offices he visited today were: ITI (Industrial Training Institute), Excise & Narcotics Office, Mizofed, Printing & Stationery Depot, and FCS & Consumer Affairs' Godown. It is intended to conduct these surprise visits whenever there is an opportunity, with the aim of visiting all offices and educational institutions under the Government of Mizoram. During his surprise visit today, the DC was accompanied by Pu Amol Srivastava, IAS, Asst. Commissioner, Pu H. Zonunmawia, Election Officer, and Pu N. Vabeiratlua, DIPRO.

reference: DISTRICT TASK FORCE COMMITTEE HELD EMERGENCY MEETING ON COVID-19 AT SIAHA District Task Force,Siaha mulled over how to take preventive measures against Covid-19 pandemic in the emergency meeting held, here at Siaha. District Magistrate had already issued prohibitory order on last Friday(7/3/2020), the order prohibited Cross- border movement between Myanmar and India through passages/roads that linked Myanmar and 10 villages within Siaha district namely: : Lopu, Chapi, Khaikhy, Zyhno,Lodaw, Lomasu, Iana, Siasi, Laki and Khopai village. The Same order highlighted that Check points will be set up at 3 villages namely: Kaochao, Tlapi and Tipi Ferry which located at Inter District Border. In pursuant to the said prohibitory Order, Siaha BDO and Tipa BDO have left for those 10 villages to call for GramSabha meeting and to sensitize about Covid-19 and Prohibitory Order. Today's meeting resolved that villagers of those 10 villages be requested to form a joint committee comprising of Church, NGOs and Village council to vigil over border passage/road that linked their respective village and Myanmar.The meeting also resolved that MADC Forest Guard and India Army stationed at villages located India-Myanmar Border be requested to help proposed village's Joint committee in their vigilant works on Border road/passage. Today's meeting also decided that on the 13th&14th March,2020 a Team comprising Medical officials, Leaders of NGOs, Joint VC members, Police personnel and DC office staff will visited those 13 villages and witness preventive measures taken by each village and carry out sensitization campaign as well. CMO & DMS informed the meeting that there was only one Thermal Infra Red Sensor and 15 Personal Protection Equipments (PPE) presently at Siaha; and 2 TIRS will arrive shortly. TIRS and Self Reporting Format will be placed at check points; and by using TIRS leh Self reporting format; suspected Covid-19 infected travellers will be identified and quarantine for 20 days.
