hypothesis:
DISTRICT TASK FORCE COMMITTEE HELD AN EMERGENCY MEETING ON COVID-19 IN SIAHA
Today at 2:00 PM, the District Task Force Committee held an emergency meeting regarding Covid-19 at the DC Conference Hall; they held a serious meeting to deliberate on how to keep Siaha district safe from Covid-19. On March 7, 2020, the District Magistrate had already closed the border crossing routes between Myanmar and 10 villages in Siaha district: Lopu, Chapi, Khaikhy, Zyhno, Lodaw, Lomasu, Iana, Siasi, Laki, and Khopai. In addition to this, an order had also been issued to set up check posts at 3 villages at the Inter-district Border crossing points: Kaochao, Tipi Ferry, and Tlapi. The Siaha BDO and Tipa BDO have also gone out today to convene Gram Sabhas and conduct sensitization campaigns in these 13 villages. Today's meeting resolved to request the formation of Joint Committees of Churches, NGOs, and VCs in each of these 13 villages, and also resolved to request these Joint Committees to monitor the border crossing routes/points between their respective villages and Myanmar. It was also resolved to invite the MADC Forest Department and the Indian military personnel stationed in the border area villages to assist them. On March 13 and 14, 2020, a joint team consisting of Medical personnel, NGO leaders, Joint VC leaders, Police, and DC office staff will visit these 13 villages to oversee how these 13 villages are monitoring the border crossing routes with Myanmar to prevent Covid-19, and will immediately follow up with a sensitization campaign. Currently, the Siaha Medical Office has only one Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS) for detecting fever and 15 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits, and it was reported that 2 more TIRS are on the way. These TIRS will be placed at the three check posts. In addition to the TIRS, the medical department will place Self-Reporting Formats at all 3 check points. Based on the TIRS and Self-Reporting Formats, travelers entering Siaha district who are suspected of potentially carrying Covid-19 will be quarantined for 20 days. Attachment Loading attachment...

reference: What then is the way to possess the good land? It is not so simple. Let us enumerate and review the steps. First of all, we must enjoy Christ as the redeeming lamb. We must receive Christ as our Savior. We must pass the judgment of God. This is the first step. If we have done this, we can put a check here; the first item has been passed. What is the second step? We must leave Egypt and enjoy Christ as our daily manna, as our daily life-supply. Of course, we cannot take food without drinking water; so at the same time we must enjoy Christ as the rock with the living water flowing forth. We enjoy the manna and we enjoy the rock with the living water. Do you have such an experience day by day? Many of you can boldly say that you do. Every day you enjoy Christ as your food and as your drink. Otherwise, you could not live, you could not go on, you could not maintain your life as a Christian. raw_text:
CHAMPHAI DISTRICT CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEE (DCC) / DISTRICT LEVEL REVIEW COMMITTEE (DLRC) MEETING No.7432/2020-2021

The Champhai District Consultative Committee (DCC)/ District Level Review Committee (DLRC) met today at the DC Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Pi Maria C.T. Zuali, Champhai DC. They reviewed the initiatives of various banks and stakeholders within the two RD Blocks of Champhai District up to the end of the September 2020 Quarter. The Deputy Commissioner, Pi Maria C.T. Zuali, also launched the Potential Linked Credit Plan (PLP) 2021-2022 for Champhai District, prepared by NABARD.

Pi Maria C.T. Zuali stated that it is necessary to bring banking facilities within everyone's reach, and emphasized the urgent need to conduct wider awareness campaigns so that eligible beneficiaries can truly receive the benefits available through banks. She urged bank officials to try to translate and provide important documents and application forms in the Mizo language so that the public can better understand how to utilize banks and comprehend the benefits available through them. She also urged them to assist the poor and those in need of upliftment so they can receive available benefits and establish themselves. Expressing concern over the wide disparity in the Credit-Deposit Ratio (the comparison between deposits and credit disbursements in banks), she urged them to be more open to achieving a better Credit-Deposit Ratio. She also urged borrowers to prioritize loan repayment, stating that the DC Office would fully support bankers in pursuing defaulters.

In this meeting, after Pu L. Lawmvela, Lead District Manager (LDM), SBI Lead Bank Office Champhai, welcomed the gathering, a review of the performance and initiatives of various banks within Champhai District up to the end of the previous September 2020 Quarter was conducted, and future plans were also discussed.

As reported in the meeting, the average Credit-Deposit (CD) Ratio comparing deposits and credit disbursements in various banks in Champhai District up to the end of the September 2020 Quarter was 44.71%. This is an increase of 2.28% compared to the CD Ratio of 42.43% at the end of the June Quarter, but it still falls short of the stipulated CD Ratio target of 60%.

Dr SK Prasad chuan Prime Minister hmathlir angin India thalaite chu space technology lamah thiamna sang zawk nei tur leh India ram chu a hmahruaitu a nih theih nan chher hriam mek an ni a ti a. reference: Governor Hari Babu and ITCA member discuss opportunities for students to learn space technology 102/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 28th June 2022: Dr SK Prasad, founder member and advisory council member, Indian Technology Congress Association ( ITCA) had called on Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati at the Raj Bhavan this forenoon. In this meeting, he and Governor discussed the opportunities for the students of higher secondary school, college and university in Mizoram to learn space technology. As proposed by his eminent guest, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati welcomed the idea of selecting students with a scientific temper to have a preliminary introduction to space science with the option to continue the advanced study depending on their performance in studies. In this regard, he advised Dr SK Prasad and the institutions he represented to have close coordination with the authorities of Higher & Technical Education Department, Mizoram University, NIT Mizoram, Polytechnics, Science & Technology Department and Science Teachers Association Of Mizoram. Dr SK Prasad apprised the Governor of their initiatives in teaching the teams of students and assigning them important science projects like making mini satellites and other space technology. He explained the importance given to horning entrepreneurship skills of the students selected in this model of learning. He told Governor that his purpose of visiting is identifying the institutions with whom they will have a series of correspondences to initiate enrollment of the students in the program. hypothesis: Governor Hari Babu and ITCA leader discuss space technology study opportunities for top students in Mizoram 1070/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 28th June 2022: This morning, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati and Dr SK Prasad, founder member and advisory council member of the Indian Technology Congress Association (ITCA), Bangalore, met at the Raj Bhavan. During this meeting, they discussed how to select outstanding students in Mizoram who wish to study space technology and how they can pursue these studies. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati stated that students in Mizoram are highly intelligent and possess the capability to compete with students from elsewhere. He expressed his belief that if opportunities to study space technology are opened up, they will be able to study it successfully. The Governor expressed his gratitude to Dr SK Prasad and the authorities at his organization for seeking out opportunities for students in Mizoram to study Space Technology. In this regard, he suggested that the ITCA leaders consult with the Higher & Technical Education Department, Mizoram University, NIT Mizoram, Polytechnics, Science & Technology Department, and the Science Teachers Association of Mizoram. He mentioned that through coordination with them, it would be easier to select the most talented students who wish to study space technology. Dr SK Prasad stated that in line with the Prime Minister's vision, Indian youth are being trained to acquire higher knowledge in space technology so that India can become a leader in this field. As part of this initiative, 75 student teams will be selected to build mini-satellites under the 75 Students' Satellites project, to be completed this year. He mentioned that students from all over India will compete for this project, and 75 teams will be selected. He added that this project would also open up opportunities for students from Mizoram to participate. Dr Prasad stated that the main purpose of his visit was to introduce the ongoing Space Technology education program for Higher Secondary to University Degree students to the students of Mizoram. In this regard, he requested the support of the Governor and state government officials, and specifically invited officials associated with science education to collaborate. raw_text:
CHAMPHAI DISTRICT TASK FORCE ON CORONA VIRUS OUTBREAK MEETS
The District Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak, constituted to keep Champhai District safe and to take precautionary measures against the Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) outbreak which is currently a major concern for China and other countries across the globe, met for the first time this afternoon at the DC Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Deputy Commissioner Pu SL Naveen, IAS.

In the meeting, it was highlighted that since Champhai District is located on the international border, there is a need to be cautious against the spread of the Novel Coronavirus. The meeting urged travelers and traders crossing the border to be cautious of the areas where the disease is currently spreading and their surroundings. During this meeting, reports on the restriction of human movement and livestock were also heard. It was also mentioned that there is a need to take steps in communication and mutual cooperation with the districts of Myanmar bordering Champhai District.

The District Task Force on Coronavirus Outbreak decided to visit villages located along the border to conduct wider awareness campaigns among the public, and to monitor the health of those entering through the border while also thoroughly tracing those who need follow-up. It was also decided that an Isolation Ward should be set up at Champhai District Hospital, and the required budget should be prepared at the earliest and submitted to the higher authorities.

The District Level Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak was constituted to take action in every district as per the wishes of the State Level Task Force on Mitigation of Corona Virus, which was formed during a meeting of the Mizoram State Health Minister and H&FW Department officials on January 30, 2020.

Medical Screening was started at Zokhawthar in Champhai District from February 4, 2020, where travelers are questioned and examined as required, and a proper Self Reporting Form has also been introduced.

The Champhai District Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak has also set up Mobile Numbers - 8588009756/9436376607 for those in need of contact.

source:
Kan ngaihthlak ang khan, September Ni 24, 2020-ah Govt. of India notification 
a awm a, chu mi dungzuiin State tinah buatsaih a ni bawk a. Amaherawhchu, tui hi State 
List a nih angin state tin sorkar chu a thu viau mai a. Tunah hian State 16 leh UT 5-ah 
he Dan hi neih a ni tawh a. Tin, State 11-ah ngaihtuah mek a ni bawk a. State 4 hi chuan 
an ramah he Dan neih hi tul an ti lova, chungte chu - Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, 
Sikkim leh Tripura te an ni. Mizoram-ah erawh chuan a tul ngawih ngawihin ka hria a. 
Amaherawhchu, control a ngai a ni. Tute’n emaw an duh duhna hmunah an pump 
chhuak rikngawt kha chu a him lova, lei hnuaia water table te pawh tibuai thei a ni. 
Chuvangin, hetianga Dan lo awm hi a tha ka ti a. Chapter 6, section 29(C)-ah khan 
hremna Dan a awm a.
reference:
As we have listened, there was a Government of India notification on September 
24, 2020, and based on that, all the states followed. But ‘water’ falls under the state list, 
so the state government has the authority. 16 states and 5 UTs currently have a similar
act regarding this, and 11 states are currently discussing this Act. Four states regarded 
it as unnecessary to have this Act, these are Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Sikkim, and 
Tripura. On the other hand, I believe Mizoram urgently requires this Act, but there must 
be a way to control it. Whoever is capable of doing it must not attempt to pump out 
water, as it could disturb the water tables. So, it is good that such acts as these exist. 
Chapter 6, Section 29 (C), talks about penalties for violators.
hypothesis: As we have heard, there was a Government of India notification on September 24, 2020, and in accordance with that, it is being prepared in every State. However, since water is on the State List, every state government has significant authority. Currently, 16 States and 5 UTs have already enacted this Law. Also, it is under consideration in 11 States. Meanwhile, 4 States do not consider it necessary to have this Law in their land, and those are - Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Sikkim, and Tripura. In Mizoram, however, I feel it is absolutely necessary. Nevertheless, control is required. It is not safe for some people to just pump it out wherever they want, as it can also disturb the underground water table. Therefore, I think it is good to have such a Law in place. In Chapter 6, Section 29(C), there is a provision for penalties.
raw_text: As we have heard, there was a Government of India notification on September 24, 2020, and in accordance with that, it is being prepared in every State. However, since water is on the State List, every state government has significant authority. Currently, 16 States and 5 UTs have already enacted this Law. Also, it is under consideration in 11 States. Meanwhile, 4 States do not consider it necessary to have this Law in their land, and those are - Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Sikkim, and Tripura. In Mizoram, however, I feel it is absolutely necessary. Nevertheless, control is required. It is not safe for some people to just pump it out wherever they want, as it can also disturb the underground water table. Therefore, I think it is good to have such a Law in place. In Chapter 6, Section 29(C), there is a provision for penalties.

hypothesis:
RASHTRIYA EKTA DIWAS CELEBRATED GRANDLY
This morning, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) was celebrated at the AR Ground, with Deputy Chief Minister Pu Tawnluia attending as the chief guest. Speaking on the occasion, Chief Guest Pu Tawnluia said that the Government of India declared October 31 as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who made immense efforts for the national integration of India. The Deputy Chief Minister stated that Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) has been celebrated since 2014, and today marks its sixth observance. He said that in 1917, after listening to a speech by the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel dedicated his utmost efforts to the Indian nation, working with great courage, and came to be called the 'Iron Man of India'. He added that when the British were about to leave India, he took the initiative to ensure that more than 500 different princely states of India could unite under India. Chief Guest Pu Tawnluia invited the gathering to work for the nation and to continue maintaining unity, just like Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who was one of the important figures among those who fought for India's freedom. Chief Secretary Pu Lalnunmawia Chuaungo administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas pledge to all those who attended the event. Nine contingents—Assam Rifles, BSF, 1st Battalion MAP, 3rd Battalion MAP, 5th IR Battalion, Home Guard, 225 Battalion CRPF, One Mizo Air Squadron NCC, and 20 Mizo Independent Company NCC—paraded, with Inspector PC Vanlalsawma, MAP, serving as the Parade Commander, and the Assam Rifles Band Party also played the National Anthem. For this celebration of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, 500 school children held a 'Run for Unity' at 7:00 AM starting from Sikulpuikawn and Chanmari, and gathered together at the AR Ground.

Hetianga internet khawvela bum tur zawng ho hian rinhlelh nachang hre lo leh bum awlsam tur zawngin, inbum dan thar an hmu chhuak reng bawk. Chuvangin hetianga inbumna laka kan himna atan Mizoram Poice chuan a hnuaia tarlan ang hian mipuite a ngen a ni: I banking password, OTP, Debit Card/Credit Card details te tumah hrilh suh. Online-a thil i lei dawnin Search Engine atanga product zawn hi a him tawk lo thin a, chuvangin online shopping website hriat chian saah ngei thil enin lei thin ang che. MIZORAM POLICE PRESS STATEMENT 566/2023-2024
The Mizoram Police Media Cell has issued the following advisory to the public regarding the Digital Payment System:

ADVISORY REGARDING DIGITAL PAYMENT FRAUD:
While our usage of Digital Payment Systems has increased significantly, fraud related to this has also risen rapidly in Mizoram itself. Fraudsters operating in this internet world are constantly finding new ways to scam people, looking for unsuspecting and easy targets. Currently, more than 75% of the Cyber Crime cases registered in Mizoram are related to 'online financial fraud'. Therefore, for our safety against such scams, the Mizoram Police appeals to the public as follows:

- Never share your banking password, OTP, or Debit Card/Credit Card details with anyone.
- Do not scan any QR Code when you are the one receiving money. No scanning is required except for the person sending the money.
- Be aware that phishing scammers are constantly trying to steal your important Bank and UPI information; do not just enter fake emails, websites, or unknown links.
- When buying things online, searching for products through Search Engines is often not safe enough; therefore, always view and buy items from well-known online shopping websites.
- Understand that offers that seem too good to be true, such as earning money with almost no work, or highly profitable yet safe investment schemes, are generally scams.
- Be cautious of applications and websites that claim to provide loans easily and quickly. They ask for all kinds of personal information to grant loans, which they later use for blackmail. Even if you use a Loan App, make sure it is authorized by the RBI.
- Also, be aware that those who pose as Police/Army personnel selling items online at very cheap rates are generally criminals.
